title.en: Lifestyle disorders: diabetes, obesity and heart disease

text.en: Greek physicians noticed that some patients passed large amounts of sweet urine. Diabetes mellitus means running through, sweet. Today it affects millions.

Lifestyle disorders are non-communicable diseases caused by improper ways of living, stress and strain.
Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder with high blood glucose due to insufficient insulin secretion or action.
Type-1 (IDDM) is juvenile onset, caused by destruction of beta-cells of the pancreas, and needs insulin; Type-2 (NIDDM) is adult onset, the cells do not respond to insulin, and it can be controlled by diet and exercise.
Symptoms: hyperglycaemia, polyuria, polydipsia, glycosuria, polyphagia, fatigue and weight loss; diagnose if fasting glucose is above 140 mg per dl.
Control: diet rich in fibre and whole grains with low refined sugar, exercise, drugs or insulin and education.
Obesity is excess body fat; BMI equals weight in kg divided by height in metres squared; 10 percent above standard weight is overweight and 20 percent is obese.
Obesity arises when calorie intake exceeds expenditure and raises the risk of hypertension, diabetes and heart disease; prevention uses low calorie diet, exercise, yoga.
Coronary heart disease is deposition of cholesterol in coronary arteries causing atherosclerosis, ischaemia and myocardial infarction.
HDL is good cholesterol and LDL is bad cholesterol; desirable blood cholesterol is less than 200 mg per dl.
Prevention: low saturated fat and salt, more fibre and PUFA, regular exercise, avoiding smoking and alcohol.

problem.en: A person is 1.6 m tall and weighs 80 kg. Calculate BMI and comment.

text.en: BMI is weight divided by height squared.
This is well above the normal range, so the person is obese and at risk.

prompt.en: Give two differences between Type-1 and Type-2 diabetes.

requiredIdeas.en: Type-2: cells do not respond, controlled by diet

points.en: LDL is bad, HDL is good cholesterol.
Exercise and diet prevent lifestyle disorders.
